title: More ways to play
summary: Limited (Draft and Sealed), the Constructed formats (Standard, Pioneer, Modern, Pauper), and where to play each.

checklist.label: I know the difference between Limited and Constructed
I know how a Booster Draft works
I know how Sealed works, and what a Prerelease is
I can tell Standard, Pioneer, Modern and Pauper apart
I know where to play each one

steps.title: Limited or Constructed?
steps.body:
Every way to play Magic is one of two kinds.

- **[[constructed|Constructed]]**: you build your deck at home from cards you own. At least 60 cards, no more than four of each. Standard and Commander are Constructed formats.
- **[[limited|Limited]]**: you open **booster packs** at the event and build a deck on the spot from what you opened. At least **40 cards**, and you may use every copy you opened.

Limited is the friendliest start: everyone has the same chance, and nobody needs a collection.

check.question: In a Limited event you open three copies of the same card. How many can go in your deck?
check.hint: The four-copy rule is a Constructed rule.

steps.title: Booster Draft
steps.body:
A [[draft|Draft]] is usually **eight players** around a table, each with **three booster packs**.

1. Everyone opens a pack, picks **one card**, and passes the rest to the left.
2. Keep picking and passing until the packs are empty.
3. Open the second pack and pass to the **right**. The third pack goes left again.
4. Build a 40-card deck from your picks, adding as many basic lands as you need.

You're choosing your deck one card at a time, while reading what the players next to you are taking.

check.question: In a Draft, after you pick a card, what happens to the rest of the pack?

options.text: You pass it to the player next to you
It goes back into the middle

steps.title: Sealed and the Prerelease
steps.body:
In [[sealed|Sealed]] you get **six booster packs**, open them all, and build a 40-card deck from the best cards you find. No passing, no picking: what you open is yours.

The most common Sealed event is the **[[prerelease|Prerelease]]**: the weekend before a new set comes out, shops run casual Sealed events so everyone can try the new cards. It's the single best first event for a new player: relaxed, and every player is learning the cards too.

check.question: What makes a Prerelease a good first event?

options.text: Everyone is new to the cards, and the deck is built from packs on the day
The prizes are the biggest of the year

check.hint: Nobody has seen the new set before.

steps.title: Building a 40-card deck
steps.body:
A Limited deck is small, so the usual shape is:

- **17 lands** and **23 other cards**, in **two colours**.
- Mostly **creatures**: about 15, with a good spread of costs from 2 to 5.
- A few **removal spells**: cards that destroy, damage or shrink a creature.

Pick your two colours from where your strongest cards are, not from what you planned to play. Shops often lend basic lands for Limited events.

visual.altText: The usual shape of a Limited deck.

check.question: How many lands do most 40-card Limited decks run?

steps.title: Standard, Pioneer, Modern
steps.body:
The main one-against-one Constructed formats differ by **which sets are allowed**:

- **[[standard|Standard]]**: the newest sets only. Older sets [[rotation|rotate]] out each year, so decks change often. Smallest card pool, easiest to start.
- **Pioneer**: every set since late 2012. No rotation. Decks stay good for years.
- **Modern**: every set since 2003. No rotation. The biggest pool and the strongest decks.

All three use 60-card decks, four copies at most, 20 life. Each has a short **banned list** of cards too strong for it.

visual.altText: Standard, Pioneer and Modern as growing card pools.

check.question: Which format changes most often because old sets leave it?

steps.title: Pauper: commons only
steps.body:
**Pauper** is Constructed with one twist: every card in your deck must have been printed at **common** rarity (the black set symbol).

- 60 cards, four copies at most, 20 life, like Standard.
- No rotation: any common from Magic's history.
- Decks are **cheap**, often the price of a single rare from another format, yet the games are sharp.

If money is the worry, Pauper is the answer. The card library in this app shows each card's rarity.

check.question: Which cards can a Pauper deck use?

options.text: Any card that costs less than a set price
Only cards from the newest sets

check.hint: It's about the rarity symbol, not the price.

steps.title: Where to play each one
steps.body:
- **MTG Arena** (free, phone and computer): Standard, Draft and Sealed with digital packs, plus casual modes. Good for learning alone.
- **Your local game store**: Prereleases, weekly Draft nights, Standard and Modern events, and Commander tables most evenings. The Wizards store locator lists them.
- **Kitchen table**: any format you and your friends agree on. Preconstructed decks make this easy.

A calm path: Arena to practise, then a Prerelease, then a Commander night.

visual.altText: Where to play, in a sensible order.

check.question: You want to try Draft without going anywhere. Where can you?

options.text: Nowhere. Draft only happens in shops
